judge.role: independent judge over the Llama Phase 3 results; Spark saw only the numbers copied from the cited files, not the files themselves

metric: gap_closed = (factored - base) / (full - base) on mean target logprob of the answer tokens; first-token accuracy reported alongside

verdicts.claim: On the combined 96 fresh items, the byte-fair variant no_embed_mlp_spread_balanced (24,515,584 B, under the 25,143,296 B budget) beats uniform_rank32: gap_closed 0.159 (15.9%) vs -0.076 (-7.6%), factored mean logprob -12.714 vs -14.201.
verdicts.note: Balanced is under budget and higher on both gap_closed and mean logprob than uniform_rank32.

verdicts.claim: The byte-fair variant wins on both halves of the fresh set: heldout24 gap_closed 0.200 vs uniform -0.017; heldout72_new 0.148 vs uniform -0.091.
verdicts.values_relied_on: heldout24: balanced gap_closed 0.200373434383912 vs uniform -0.016714667787171608; heldout72_new: balanced 0.14817956351361586 vs uniform -0.09109894297869517
verdicts.note: Balanced gap_closed exceeds uniform on both fresh subsets.

verdicts.claim: uniform_rank32's combined-96 factored mean logprob (-14.201) is below the base model's own score (-13.718): on this pair the human recipe makes fresh-item scores worse than no patch at all.
verdicts.values_relied_on: uniform_rank32 mean -14.20128408199294 vs base mean -13.717832809408115; higher logprob is better
verdicts.note: Uniform_rank32 mean is more negative than base, so worse than no patch.

verdicts.claim: The Stage 2 winner no_embed_mlp_spread (gap_closed 0.403 on the 24 probe questions) is byte-unfair: 34,690,048 bytes is +38.0% over the 25,143,296-byte budget; uniform's Stage 2 gap_closed is 0.088.
verdicts.values_relied_on: no_embed_mlp_spread gap_closed 0.4029778971569745, 34690048 bytes vs budget 25143296 bytes (+38.0%); uniform_rank32 gap_closed 0.08834323479864378, 25143296 bytes
verdicts.note: Stage 2 winner exceeds the byte budget by ~38% while uniform gap is 0.088.

verdicts.claim: No factored config on the 96 outscores the full delta (best factored -12.123 vs full -7.387), every factored gap_closed on this pair is below 1.0, and first-token accuracy stays low for every factored config (best 3.1% vs full delta 21.9%); so gap_closed remains a true recovery fraction on this pair, and overall recovery here (byte-fair 15.9%) is weaker than on pair 1 (Qwen byte-fair 23.2% on the same 96).
verdicts.note: In-pair recovery facts match, but the pair-1 Qwen 23.2% comparison has no numbers provided to judge against.
verdicts.resolution: Investigated the same day: the NOT SUPPORTED is a scope limit, not a factual dispute. Spark confirmed every in-pair fact in claim E (best factored -12.123 vs full -7.387, all gap_closed below 1.0, best factored accuracy 3.1% vs full 21.9%) and objected only that the pair-1 Qwen 23.2% figure was not in the numbers it was shown. That figure stands on its own records: results/alien_sweep_heldout96.json (gap_closed 0.231923) and the earlier Spark judging addendum, claim A, which that same judge marked SUPPORTED. The README wording therefore keeps the in-pair facts and the cross-pair comparison, each resting on its own pair's records.

summary: Claims A-D are fully supported by the cited files, while E fails because its cross-pair Qwen comparison is outside the provided numbers.
